# git: alias: add rewrite command to reword the last commit

Add `git rewrite`, which changes the message of the last commit and nothing else. **Motivation:** typos, wrong scopes and references resolved after the fact need fixing without moving the commit in time — plain `git commit --amend` resets the committer date to now, which shifts the commit in the contributions calendar and in date-based tooling. `git amend` ([[DOT-352]]) preserves both dates but is `--no-edit` by design: it folds staged changes in. There was no "reword only".

```bash
$ git rewrite 'fix(git): keep both dates on amend'      # message from arguments
$ git rewrite <<<'message with "quotes" and `backticks`' # from stdin
$ git rewrite                                           # on a terminal: editor
```

Decisions: both dates survive (`--date=%aI` for the author, `GIT_COMMITTER_DATE=%cI` for the committer); `--only` with no paths rewrites the message alone, so staged changes stay in the index — the deliberate difference from `git amend`; argument/stdin semantics copied from `git-commit`/`git-contrib` (`"${*}"`, `-F -` when stdin is not a terminal), stdin being the way to pass a body with both quote characters. Out of scope: arbitrary commits via `--fixup=reword:` ([[DOT-181]]), changing the author ([[DOT-230]]), interactive range rewrites.
